hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.
A: APOE genotype or apoE isoform (APOE4 vs APOE3)
B: binding/adhesion strength of apoE to recycling receptors (ApoER2, LRP1, LDLR, VLDLR...) and the resulting impeded receptor recycling
scope: IN: binding strength or kinetics of apoE isoforms to recycling receptors (ApoER2/LRP8, LRP1, LDLR, VLDLR, heparan sulfate when tied to receptor recycling), pH-dependent dissociation in endosomes, and receptor surface levels/recycling impeded by apoE4 (e.g. ApoER2, glutamate receptors trapped in endosomes), including rescues (NHE6 inhibition) in apoE4 conditions. OUT: receptor-independent effects, binding to non-recycling partners, downstream synaptic function without a receptor-recycling readout.

row.Finding description: Insulin increased IR-GFP colocalization with transferrin after apoE3 treatment but produced no significant increase after apoE4 treatment in three independent experiments.
row.Finding quote: Insulin induced IR internalization which increased the co-localization of IR-GFP with transferrin in apoE3-treated cells, but not in apoE4-treated cells (Figures 6A and 6D).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (reduced insulin-induced increase in endosomal insulin receptor)

row.Finding description: After insulin-induced internalization, intracellular insulin receptor declined with apoE3 but showed no obvious decline with apoE4, consistent with impaired recycling.

The legend reports 15–18 cells per condition in replicate experiments.

proposed.why: Receptor localization in early/recycling compartments (or cellular apoE-receptor association) is a surrogate B' for trapping, scored class 3, strength 3 like every other such colocalization row. (was 3/2)

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments in primary mouse neurons treated with Reelin, adding human ApoE4 reduced surface ApoER2 compared with the condition without added apoE.
row.Finding quote: ApoE-conditioned media treatment reduces the surface expression of Apoer2 and glutamate receptors in presence of Reelin in primary neurons. Receptor surface levels show a stronger reduction with ApoE4 than ApoE3.
row.Finding summary: (No added apoE -> added ApoE4) -> (lower neuronal surface ApoER2 during Reelin stimulation)
row.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from E18 Slc9a6 wildtype mouse embryos, assayed at DIV10–14; no AD-model mutation reported. Human ApoE4 was supplied in HEK293 conditioned medium at 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes before a further 30-minute Reelin treatment at 2 μg/ml; the comparator lacked added apoE. Surface ApoER2 was measured by surface biotinylation, NeutrAvidin isolation, and immunoblotting. The endpoint assesses surface availability associated with recycling, without measuring receptor–apoE binding or dissociation; these were mouse brain cells.

proposed.why: Comparator is no added apoE, not apoE3, so apoE4 addition is a surrogate A' (any apoE ligand drives receptor internalization, shown in P7) and surface/internalized receptor is a surrogate B': class 4, strength 4. (was 2/3)

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, germline NHE6 deletion restored ApoE4-impaired surface GluN2B expression in primary mouse neurons treated with Reelin.
row.Finding quote: In addition, genetic loss of NHE6 equally restored the ApoE4-impaired surface expression of AMPA and NMDA receptor subunits (Figure 4D–F).
row.Finding summary: (NHE6 present -> NHE6 deleted, with ApoE4) -> (restored neuronal surface GluN2B)
row.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from E18 germline Slc9a6-knockout mouse embryos and wildtype littermates, assayed at DIV10–14; no AD-model mutation reported. Human ApoE4 from HEK293 conditioned medium was applied at 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes, followed by Reelin at 2 μg/ml for another 30 minutes. Surface GluN2B was measured by biotinylation and immunoblotting. This tests rescue of co-trafficked receptor surface availability in mouse neurons, without measuring apoE–receptor binding or neuronal endosomal pH.

proposed.why: A is held at APOE4 and a path variable (NHE6/endosomal pH) is manipulated, which does not perturb A even as a surrogate, so class 5 (rescue tests mediation, not A->B); strength one step below the matching isoform readout. (was 2/3)

row.Finding description: APOER2 late-endosomal colocalization showed no significant difference between genotypes, despite a reported 22.09% decrease in APOE4 neurons; 25–37 cells from two to three preparations were analyzed.
row.Finding quote: This decrease in late endosomes was significant for both IR and VEGFR with a similar trend observed in APOER2 (IR: 25.80% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 47.74% decrease, p < 0.05; APOER2 : 22.09% decrease, p = 0.156).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in APOER2 colocalization with late endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; APOER2/Rab7 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

proposed.why: Late-endosome/lysosome colocalization is weakly coupled to recycling (degradation is an alternative route), so class 3, strength 4, same for every receptor in this assay. (was 3/3)

row.Finding description: APOER2 knockdown reduced insulin-receptor early-endosomal colocalization in APOE4 neurons by 55.1%, assessed in 34–38 cells from three preparations.
row.Finding quote: A different pattern was observed with the growth factor receptors IR and VEGFR, where knocking down APOER2 increased the levels of IR (50.9% increase relative to APOE4 control) and VEGFR (21.3% increase relative to APOE4 control) in APOE4 neurons and decreased their colocalization with early endosomes (IR: 55.1% reduction, and VEGFR: 52.6% reduction relative to APOE4 control).
row.Finding summary: (APOER2 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (lower fraction of insulin receptor colocalizing with early endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 APOER2 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; insulin-receptor/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.

row.Finding description: LRP1 knockdown reduced insulin-receptor early-endosomal colocalization in APOE4 neurons by 48.9%, assessed in 34–40 cells from four preparations.
row.Finding quote: As can be seen, the downregulation of LRP1 had no significant effects on the total levels of the receptors, had no effect on the size of early endosomes (not shown), but did abolish the excess colocalization of these receptors with early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (the percent of reduction when compared to APOE4 control equals to 38.8% in APOER2, 48.9% in IR, and 64.1% in VEGFR).
row.Finding summary: (LRP1 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (lower fraction of insulin receptor colocalizing with early endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 LRP1 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; insulin-receptor/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.

row.Finding description: Insulin-receptor surface-to-total ratio showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons, despite a reported 28.77% reduction in APOE4 across three cohorts.
row.Finding quote: Similar, though less prominent, pattern was evident in IR (Fig. 4 C, 28.77% reduction, p = 0.07), and VEGFR (Fig. 4D, 9.90% reduction, p = 0.15).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in neuronal insulin-receptor surface-to-total ratio)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; surface biotinylation at 4°C and receptor ELISA; three pooled-pup cohorts.

proposed.why: Isoform varied but the readout is steady surface level of an apoE-binding receptor, a surrogate B' for impeded recycling (endocytosis or synthesis could also move it), so class 3, strength 2, same as every other surface-level row. (was 3/3)

row.Finding description: VEGFR2 late-endosomal colocalization was 47.74% lower in APOE4 than APOE3 neurons, measured in 25–37 cells from two to three preparations.
row.Finding quote: This decrease in late endosomes was significant for both IR and VEGFR with a similar trend observed in APOER2 (IR: 25.80% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 47.74% decrease, p < 0.05; APOER2 : 22.09% decrease, p = 0.156).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower fraction of VEGFR2 colocalizing with late endosomes)

proposed.why: Late-endosome/lysosome colocalization is weakly coupled to recycling (degradation is an alternative route), so class 3, strength 4, same for every receptor in this assay. (was 3/3)

row.Finding description: Without axotomy, adding human apoE4 was reported not to substantially change surface LRP8 relative to no added human apoE, with no significant difference reported or comparison-specific P supplied.
row.Finding quote: Without injury, excess human ApoE did not substantially alter surface LRP8 level or Src activation (Fig. 4K, 4M and 4N).
row.Finding summary: (no added human apoE -> added apoE4, without axotomy) -> (no change in surface LRP8)
row.Experimental system: Uninjured primary cortical neurons from P1 wild-type mice, retaining endogenous mouse ApoE; purified human apoE4 lipoparticles, 12 µg/ml, versus no exogenous human apoE; reelin, 2 µg/ml for 1 hour; day-12 surface biotinylation and LRP8 immunoblot.

row.Finding description: Adding apoE4 reduced cell-surface ApoER2 by 50% relative to untreated controls in mouse N2a-APPsw cells, averaged over two experiments.
row.Finding quote: Compared with controls, the remaining cell-surface ApoER2, APP, and β-secretase decreased by ∼25, 25, and 7%, respectively, when ApoE was added and 50, 50, and 35%, respectively, when ApoE4 was present ( Fig. 2 a ).
row.Finding summary: (no added apoE4 -> added apoE4) -> (lower cell-surface ApoER2)
row.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably expressing human Swedish-mutant APP, supplied by Dr. Riqiang Yan, transiently transfected with murine ApoER2 and human β-secretase using Lipofectamine 2000. Twenty-four hours after transfection, cells received 10 μg/ml apoE4 for 2 h. Remaining surface proteins were labeled with sulfo-NHS-LC-biotin at 4°C, recovered with NeutrAvidin agarose, and quantified by Western blot densitometry relative to total cellular protein. This was not a human brain-cell system.

proposed.why: Comparator is no added apoE, not apoE3, so apoE4 addition is a surrogate A' (any apoE ligand drives receptor internalization, shown in P7) and surface/internalized receptor is a surrogate B': class 4, strength 4. (was 3/3)

row.Finding description: In three repeated human-fibroblast competition experiments with four wells per condition, APOE4-mouse VLDL competed more strongly than APOE3-mouse VLDL for human LDL receptor binding and internalization, with Ki values of 3.6 ± 0.6 mg versus 5.7 ± 1.12 mg.
row.Finding quote: K i determined from 3 repeated experiments, each consisting of quadruple measurements, were 3.6 ± 0.6 mg for 4/4 VLDL and 5.7 ± 1.12 mg for 3/3 VLDL (P = 0.05 by one-way ANOVA). Therefore, the 4/4 VLDL has the ability to compete with human LDL for binding to the human LDL receptor better than the 3/3 VLDL.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4 in donor mice) -> (lower VLDL competition Ki for human LDL receptor binding and internalization)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized human fibroblasts supplied by J. Herz, exposed at 37°C to fluorescently labeled human LDL (50 μg/mL) and competing VLDL (0.5–100 μg/mL total protein). VLDL was isolated from plasma pooled from at least six female mice per genotype: human APOE3- or APOE4-targeted-replacement F2 129 × C57BL/6 hybrids, generally 8–20 weeks old, maintained on an HFC diet containing 15.8% fat, 1.25% cholesterol, and 0.5% sodium cholate. Cells received DMEM with 0.5% BSA for 24 hours before the assay. Cellular fluorescence measured LDL association and internalization. Brain cells and receptor recycling were not examined.
row.Data location: Fig 1b; Results, Production of functional apo E4 in mice with human APOE*4

proposed.why: Binding of whole native lipoproteins from genotype-differing donors is a surrogate B' for apoE-receptor adhesion (apoB and particle composition also change), so class 3, strength 3 for all native-particle rows. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: At 0.125 mg, full-length apoE–DMPC reduced bound ³H-LDL by 39–42% across the two isoforms. The authors described no overall isoform specificity. They gave no dose-specific significance test.
row.Finding quote: The full-length apoE proteins with DMPC showed dose-de- pendent competing ability, whereas a 2.5-fold dose of apoE-DMPC complex lowered 39–42% of the bound 3H-LDL and 20-fold dose low- ered 81–83% (Fig. 5
row.Finding summary: Full-length apoE3 and apoE4 showed similar observed LDLR competition at 0.125 mg with DMPC.
row.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatoblastoma cells; recombinant human full-length apoE expressed in E. coli with a C-terminal His tag, complexed with DMPC; 0.125 mg competitor; cells serum-starved for 24 h, then incubated with 3H-LDL and competitor at 4 °C for 2 h; cell-associated radiolabel measured. Brain cells, affinity constants, endosomal dissociation and receptor recycling were not examined.

row.Finding description: Without DMPC, full-length apoE3 and apoE4 each decreased ³H-LDL binding by 34%. Table 4 gives apoE4 100% of apoE3’s normalized binding ability. The authors supplied no between-isoform significance test.
row.Finding quote: The LDL-R binding ability of apoE- DMPC was higher than that of LDL at the same dose (20-fold), although apoE with or without DMPC did not show isoform specificity.
row.Finding summary: Full-length apoE3 and apoE4 gave identical reported LDLR competition without DMPC.
row.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatoblastoma cells; 0.5 mg E. coli-expressed, C-terminally His-tagged human full-length apoE without DMPC; 24 h serum starvation followed by competitive 3H-LDL binding at 4 °C for 2 h. No endosomal dissociation or receptor-recycling assay.

row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (higher Kd and weaker binding to WT-LRPIV)
row.Experimental system: Cell-free binding ELISA using commercial apoE3 and apoE4 from Invitrogen and purified, untagged human WT-LRPIV expressed in CHO cells from a construct derived from human spleen RNA; immobilized receptor coating concentration 5 μg/ml; ligand incubation for 2 hours at room temperature in HBSC, pH 7.4, containing 0.05% Tween 20; apparent Kd fitted by nonlinear one-site binding regression. row.Finding description: In quadruplicate J774 macrophage binding assays, recombinant apoE3- and apoE4-enriched VLDL both efficiently competed with radiolabelled LDL for receptor binding; no significant difference between apoE4 and apoE3 was reported, although no statistical comparison was provided.
row.Finding quote: Each VLDL particle competed efficiently (fig. 4), except for the recombinant apolipoprotein E2 complex and apolipoprotein E deficient VLDL, as ex- pected.

row.Experimental system: Mouse J774 macrophage cell line; human recombinant apoE3 and apoE4 expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3) as fusion proteins with a 42-amino-acid amino-terminal extension. ApoE-deficient VLDL isolated from apoE-knockout mice were separately enriched with each isoform for 1 hour at 37 °C and separated from free apoE by ultracentrifugation. Following 20 hours in medium containing lipid-free human serum, macrophages underwent quadruplicate competition incubations with 125I-labelled LDL and unlabelled competitors for 3 hours on melting ice. Cell-associated radioactivity measured LDL binding. Recombinant apoE loading differed between the VLDL preparations; receptor recycling was not measured.
